old: In Hungarian, expressing nuanced beliefs involves nesting causal clauses under mental evaluation verbs (*gondol, vél, hisz, tart*). The primary matrix uses an anticipatory demonstrative pronoun (*azt gondolom, úgy vélem, amellett vagyok*), followed by *hogy* and an explanatory conjunction like *mert* or *mivel*.
new: You know *azt hiszem, hogy* and *szerintem* from A2 Unit 12, and *mert* from A1. Here you add more ways to open an opinion (*azt gondolom, hogy …*, *úgy vélem, hogy …*, *amellett vagyok, hogy …*) and a reason after it with *mert*, *mivel* or *hiszen*.
why: presents the A2 pattern azt hiszem, hogy + mert as new without a recap; the "anticipatory demonstrative" description is the B2 family b2-cataphoric-clauses

old: Rather than flat agreement or disagreement, B1 Hungarian uses degree adverbs to calibrate commitment:
new: You know *Részben egyetértek, de …* from B1 Unit 41 and adverbs in -an/-en from A2 Unit 19. To say how far you agree, add more degree words:
why: recap: részben egyetértek is B1 Unit 41; -an/-en adverbs are A2 Unit 19

old: To weigh conflicting perspectives, Hungarian pairs correlative adverbs: *egyrészt... másrészt...* (on the one hand... on the other hand...) or the more formal *egyfelől... másfelől...*. Each coordinate clause presents a distinct argument.
new: You know *egyrészt … másrészt …* from B1 Unit 7 and *egyfelől … másfelől …* from B1 Unit 25. To weigh two sides of a question, give one argument in each clause: *egyrészt... másrészt...* (on the one hand... on the other hand...) or the more formal *egyfelől... másfelől...*.
why: presents egyrészt … másrészt (B1 Unit 7) and egyfelől … másfelől (B1 Unit 25) as new

old: To pivot between contrasting arguments within nuanced discussions, Hungarian uses post-positive *viszont* (however), literary *ellenben* (by contrast), and dignified *mindazonáltal* (nevertheless).
new: You know *viszont* from B1 Unit 21 and *mindazonáltal* from B1 Unit 35. New here is *ellenben* (by contrast), a literary word that works like *viszont*. Both usually stand after the word they contrast; *mindazonáltal* (nevertheless) opens its clause.
why: presents viszont (Unit 21) and mindazonáltal (Unit 35) as new

old: In sophisticated argumentation, conceding a valid counterpoint strengthens one's credibility. Hungarian uses *bár... mégis* (although... still), *jóllehet* (even though), or *noha* (albeit). The subordinate clause introduces the concession while the main clause asserts the primary thesis.
new: You know *bár*, *habár* and *annak ellenére, hogy* from B1 Unit 9. *Noha* and *jóllehet* work the same way, and you have met them in earlier units. Admitting a fair point makes your own view stronger: *bár... mégis* (although... still), *jóllehet* (even though), *noha* (albeit). The first clause admits the point and the main clause, often with *mégis*, gives your view.
why: presents bár/noha/jóllehet (B1 Unit 9, Unit 35) as new

old: To attach conditions to one's agreement, use *azzal a feltétellel / kikötéssel, hogy...* (on the condition that...) or formal conditional *amennyiben... úgy...* (insofar as... then...).
new: You know *ha* and *amennyiben* from A2 Unit 13, and *feltéve, hogy* from B1 Unit 55. To attach a condition to your agreement, say what you support and then name your *fenntartás* (reservation) or *megkötés* (condition), or use the formal *amennyiben* (= *ha*, if); the main clause may then begin with *úgy* (then).
why: amennyiben (A2 Unit 13) is not "insofar as"; azzal a feltétellel/kikötéssel in the text does not match the examples; the azzal a …, hogy anchor is the B2 family b2-cataphoric-clauses; amennyiben ... úgy ... pair is not in the examples

old: Támogatom a javaslatot azzal a fenntartással, hogy átlátható marad a végrehajtás.
new: Támogatom a javaslatot, de van egy fenntartásom: legyen átlátható a végrehajtás.
why: example 1 uses the anchor azzal a fenntartással, hogy (B2 family b2-cataphoric-clauses); the text named a different phrase

old: To actively dismantle a counterargument, formal Hungarian uses *ezzel szemben úgy vélem, hogy...* (in contrast to this I hold that...) or the idiomatic rejection *nem állja meg a helyét az az állítás, hogy...* (the assertion that... does not hold water).
new: You know *ezzel szemben* from B1 Unit 21 and *cáfol* from B1 Unit 25. New here is the idiom *nem állja meg a helyét* (does not hold water). To answer a claim, say *ezzel szemben úgy vélem, hogy...* (in contrast to this I believe that...) or *nem állja meg a helyét a vád, hogy...* (the accusation that... does not hold water).
why: presents ezzel szemben (Unit 21) as new; az az állítás, hogy is the cataphoric anchor of the B2 family b2-cataphoric-clauses (and az a + noun)

old: When defending an argument with confidence, speakers deploy modal disjuncts such as *kétségkívül* (undoubtedly), *minden bizonnyal* (in all probability / most certainly), *nyilvánvalóan* (obviously), and *vitathatatlanul* (indisputably).
new: You know *kétségkívül* and *nyilvánvalóan* from B1 Unit 30, and *minden bizonnyal* from B1 Unit 43. New here is *vitathatatlanul* (indisputably). Use these words when you are sure of your argument: *kétségkívül* (undoubtedly), *minden bizonnyal* (in all probability), *nyilvánvalóan* (obviously), *vitathatatlanul* (indisputably).
why: presents kétségkívül, nyilvánvalóan (Unit 30) and minden bizonnyal (Unit 43) as new; "most certainly" overstates minden bizonnyal; "disjuncts" is jargon
